rationale.conceptual: The paper's own custom method (exact single-ion anisotropy treatment in a rotated frame, RPA decoupling, operator-reduction identities, self-consistent angle determination) requires deep understanding of the derivation and non-trivial translation into code: matrix construction, diagonalization, 2D integration, and convergence loops. Several interacting components, not a standard textbook recipe.
rationale.execution: The reproduction comprises two independent runs of the same Python script (one per parameter set) to produce CSV files. No multi-stage pipeline, no data acquisition, no complex tooling; only standard libraries numpy/scipy and straightforward I/O.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing a non-trivial many-body Green's function formalism from a theoretical condensed-matter paper: constructing the non-symmetric matrix, Brillouin-zone integration, self-consistent angle condition, and exact treatment of single-ion anisotropy via higher-order Green's functions. The method is not a standard library call but a custom, multi-component algorithm needing careful derivation translation, making it conceptually challenging (4). Execution is trivial: a single Python script run twice with different parameters, no multi-step pipeline or data fetching (1). Resource needs are minimal—CPU-only, tiny matrices, no data.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Purely CPU-based; solves small (4x4) matrix eigenvalue problems per (k, iteration), integrates over a 2D Brillouin zone, and performs self-consistent iterations for a monolayer. No dataset loading; memory footprint negligible.
